title: Commercial interests shaping state policy
description: Commercial actors and governments can have overlapping interests; the two cases show different documented channels, not a universal causal rule.

title: Privatized gains, socialized risk
description: British parliamentary intervention followed the East India Company's financial crisis, providing a case for investigating risk allocation and accountability.

title: Covert intervention and long-term blowback
description: The 1953 Iranian coup allows the long-term political consequences of covert intervention to be investigated; specific causal effects remain under review.

title: Imperial fiscal stress, corporate relief and contested legitimacy
description: The same empire faced state debt, colonial taxation disputes and an East India Company financial crisis. Overlapping policies affected different groups differently, without requiring one unified secret plan.
